title: Choose Taracine's visual world
question: The roll assigned Avenida Marquee. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Avenida Marquee
options.lineage: 1930s–50s Manila movie palaces: the Metropolitan Theater, the Ideal, State, Lyric and Capitol on Rizal Avenue
options.thesis: The whole site is one deco theater facade: blade sign, changeable-letter canopy board, brass ticket booth.
options.viewport: A vertical TARACINE blade sign with a bulb chase stands at the left edge; across the top runs the black-and-white changeable-letter canopy board spelling tonight's titles and times; beneath it a brass-grilled ticket-booth strip holds the finder (Cinema · Date · Movie · Buy tickets); the first poster row sits under the canopy in stepped deco frames on salmon stucco.
options.risk: Deco ornament can swallow dense showtime data; the stucco and brass stay flat and hard-edged or the page turns into a costume.

raised.raise: Medium discipline: every rule, bulb and frame sits on a hard 4px grid, no soft shadows anywhere, only brass hairlines and flat enamel.
The clock is visible: every showtime strip carries a live NOW marker and past times fall dark, locked to real time like a chase light.
Strict horizontal courses: marquee, canopy board, booth, poster row stack as full-width bands; no floating cards break a course.

options.label: Karatula Billboard
options.lineage: hand-painted movie billboards of Rizal Avenue and Recto, sign-painter enamel on plywood
options.thesis: Every film is a hand-painted billboard; what's showing is spelled by a sign painter, not a template.
options.viewport: One giant painted billboard of the lead film fills the viewport, title brush-lettered with a hard offset shadow and a stapled NOW SHOWING ribbon; the finder is a painted plank sign bolted across the bottom edge.
options.risk: Also the most familiar 'retro poster' landing for a cinema brand, and without image generation the painted art has to be faked in CSS, where it collapses into filters.

options.label: Fly-posted Hoarding
options.lineage: screenprinted street-fair flyers pasted layer on layer over a hoarding
options.thesis: The homepage is a wall of pasted posters with one calm white ticket panel floating on top.
options.viewport: Full-bleed collage of film posters pasted at angles, a lime pill CTA, the brand word broken into a different colour per letter, and the white finder card floating centre-right; a purple marquee band repeats NOW SHOWING between chevrons.
options.case: Very Manila: fly-posted walls are how the city announces everything, and the floating finder panel maps cleanly onto the cinema picker. Loses on clarity: a collage ground competes with the posters that are the content.
options.risk: Reads as a festival, not a cinema chain, when the posters are not real artwork.

options.label: Hand-processed 16mm
options.lineage: hand-processed 16mm strips with scratches, uneven chemistry and light leaks
options.thesis: The catalog is a film strip; the active frame blooms orange with a light leak.
options.viewport: A horizontal strip of poster frames with sprocket margins runs across the viewport; the selected film's frame flares orange; edge-code caps label Now Showing / Coming Soon; the finder sits in the leader below.
options.case: Cinema-native and gorgeous; holds audience identification because it is literally the medium. Loses on clarity: grain and scratches fight poster legibility and showtime tables.
options.risk: Arthouse register for a mall multiplex audience; the artifacts read as a filter if not tied to real frames.

options.label: Ligne Claire Album
options.lineage: Brussels clear-line adventure albums: one even black line, flat unshadowed colour
options.thesis: Every film is a panel in a strict album grid; red is saved for the buy action.
options.viewport: A wide establishing panel opens the page (tonight's headline film), then poster panels ranked in a four-tier waffle grid; the finder is a yellow caption box; the active panel keeps full colour while its tier rests one tone paler.
options.case: Holds product clarity: flat fills, strict grid and one red action are unbeatable for scanning. Loses on identification: the Brussels album is not the Filipino moviegoer's own shelf.
options.risk: Hand-lettered balloons on commercial UI slide into whimsy.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit desktop with dithered grays and window chrome
options.thesis: Films as windows on a dithered desktop.
options.viewport: Overlapping film windows on a gray dither ground.
options.case: Dithering destroys poster art and Filipino moviegoers do not identify with a 1984 desktop.
options.kept: Hard-grid medium discipline: no soft shadows, whole-pixel rules.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm machine step row with a chase light
options.thesis: Showtimes as sixteen step keys under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step showtime row with a sweeping chase light.
options.case: The step row is a clever showtime strip, but the instrument panel says nothing about movies to this audience.
options.kept: A live NOW marker on every time strip; past times fall dark.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.lineage: monumental coiled clay tower with visible courses
options.thesis: The page rises in horizontal clay courses.
options.viewport: Content banded in coil courses up a tower.
options.case: No connection to moviegoing, and terracotta bands hide poster art.
options.kept: Strict horizontal courses: full-width bands, no floating cards.

canonCard.label: The cinema-chain standard
canonCard.thesis: What cinema chains ship: a dark UI, poster carousels, one red Buy Tickets button, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Trailer-still hero with a red CTA, a horizontal poster carousel, Now Showing / Coming Soon tabs, cinema dropdown.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every streaming and multiplex site by design, and closest to what the brief asked to move away from.
